title: Agent Client Protocol becomes default coding-agent interop standard by H1 2027
body: Cognition's decision to retire the Windsurf brand and reopen the editor as Devin Desktop - rebuilt from an editor-with-AI into an agent manager whose default surface hosts Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode, any third-party ACP agent, and a team's own in-house agents over the open Agent Client Protocol - reframes the coding tool as a neutral host rather than a vehicle for one company's model. ACP is already described as adopted by JetBrains, Google, GitHub and 25-plus agents, which is the signature of a protocol crossing from one vendor's convenience into shared infrastructure: the editor, the orchestration layer, and the underlying agent are being decoupled so none is locked to a single vendor. The strongest forward thesis from this week is that the open agent-interop layer - ACP or an equivalent cross-vendor protocol - hardens into the de-facto standard that coding-agent tools converge on, the way LSP became the universal editor-to-language-server contract. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one major code editor or IDE that is NOT Cognition (the strongest candidates being a JetBrains IDE, VS Code or a VS Code fork, Zed, or a Google developer surface) ships first-class, default support for ACP - or a materially equivalent open agent-interop protocol that lets a user run an arbitrary third-party coding agent in-editor - rather than only its own first-party agent, and the published roster of ACP-compatible agents grows past 50. If no non-Cognition IDE has shipped default open-protocol agent support and the agent count has not crossed 50 by June 30, 2027, the prediction fails. The counter-risk is that platform owners instead entrench vertically integrated, first-party agent stacks - the Project Polaris pattern of swapping in an in-house model - and treat cross-vendor interop as a checkbox rather than the default surface.

reasoning.because: Devin Desktop, JetBrains, Google, GitHub + 25 agents already wire editors to any agent over open ACP
reasoning.given: Cognition retired Windsurf for an agent-neutral ACP IDE, decoupling the editor from any one vendor
reasoning.so_that: a second major IDE adopts ACP (or an equivalent open agent-interop protocol) as a default agent surface
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027: a non-Cognition IDE ships ACP by default; 50+ ACP agents
reasoning.plain_language: The way code editors talk to AI helpers is becoming one shared standard, so any editor can run any AI agent.

summary: Cognition retired Windsurf for the agent-neutral Devin Desktop, on open Agent Client Protocol that runs Codex, Claude Agent and 25-plus agents and is adopted by JetBrains, Google and GitHub. Expect an open agent-interop protocol to become the default cross-vendor coding-agent standard by H1 2027.
